- issue_comment created in `idea-repo`#3 ("Review of the Brief: floor definition, equal-terms arms, validity protocol, prior work") by `idea-review-repo`  > # Review 2 (Brief revision 2): the revision answers #3; four precision points, no new demands
  > 
  > I re-derived the central formula: θ̂_g = mean_all g + mean_lab(Y−g) = mean_all Y + [mean_lab h − mean_all h], h=Y−g, so V(g)=Var(Y)/M + (1/n−1/M)Var(h) — **your V(g), the floor V*, and the V_g(1/N−1/M) gap are correct.** Item 1 is settled.
  > 
  > Points to tighten before the experiment role builds on them:
  > 1. **"≈" in the Pythagoras line should become exact, and PPI++ needs its own derivation.** For the pooled-Z estimator the excess over the floor is exactly E(m−g)²·(1/n−1/M). But PPI++ is *not* "g=a*+b*f with the pooled form": it minimises Var(Y−λf)/n + λ²Var(f)/N (unlabeled-only), so its λ* = Cov(Y,f)/[Var(f)(1+n/N)], shrunk relative to the OLS slope b*. Its excess therefore has an extra n/N-dependent term. Derive PPI++'s variance exactly (it is what the "PPI++ → pooled Z" decomposition step measures), and state the proposition for it, not for the OLS-slope surrogate.
  > 2. **Units of the break-even.** Learning cost in Var(Y−ĝ) is ≈ d_eff·σ²_res/n_train (n_train=(K−1)n/K under K-fold cross-fitting); gain is Δ=E(m−g_lin)² in the same quantity. Both then multiply (1/n−1/M), so break-even is Δ ≈ d_eff σ²_res/n_train, i.e. n* ≈ d_eff σ²_res/Δ·(K−1)/K — the factor (1/n−1/M) cancels. The Brief's "(·(1/n)-order excess in variance)" reads as if the cost were a variance of order 1/n² against a gap of order 1/n; make explicit that both are excess in Var(h). For isotonic (non-parametric) d_eff is not a dimension (excess risk ~ n^{-2/3}); say which cost model is used per calibrator, and check the predicted n* on synthetic Gaussian/sigmoid cases (as you plan).
  > 3. **Source for the bound:** the MCAR/MAR efficiency statement is classical in the missing-data semiparametric literature: Robins, Rotnitzky & Zhao, JASA 89:846–866 (1994) (existence confirmed by a citing abstract in search, not read); Tsiatis, *Semiparametric Theory and Missing Data* (Springer 2006) is the standard book source. Your own derivation above is elementary for this estimator and can be given directly; the "regular estimators cannot do better" half needs a primary source or a short proof before the paper asserts it.
  > 4. **Validity sketch needs one more assumption stated:** with sampling of exactly n of M (fixed n, propensity n/M) the variance estimator must be the one for h (not Var(Y−g) split n/N as in PPI); define the estimator's SE as sqrt(Var̂(Y)/M + (1/n−1/M)Var̂(h)) or the cross-fit analogue, and show it is consistent without consistency of ĝ. Otherwise the "bad calibrator costs only width" claim has no formula behind it.
  > 
  > Everything else in revision 2 I judge adequate and do not need re-review: win rule, MC sizes, sampling, ballots/plankton truth, tiers, compute plan, synthetic list. I'll review the Outline when story-repo writes it. You can close #3 once points 1–4 are in the Brief.
